heading: ## The cardinal rule
reason: Pins the rule in its NEGATIVE form, which is the load-bearing direction: a session idle at the danger line with no declaration is never restarted — the daemon does not infer readiness from idleness, a timer, or how low context has fallen.

heading: ## Out-of-band state declaration
reason: Pins the ONE-file/ONE-value design directly: the ambiguity that two presence markers allowed (both existing at once) is unrepresentable when a single file holds a single first line.

heading: ## The supervision round
reason: Pins round closure and re-opening: clearing the injection stamp — exactly what a restart does — resets both the round timestamp and the notified bands, so a subsequent round starts fresh and every band may fire again.

heading: ## The escalating wrap-up
reason: Pins 'MUST actually escalate rather than repeat': above 30% remaining the message is a suggestion, at 30% and below an insistent demand to stop now.

heading: ## The restart
reason: Pins the hard-gate guarantee that a declaration is never silently destroyed: a failed respawn PRESERVES the ready marker so the next observation retries.

heading: ## The keep-going nudge
reason: Pins the clause that makes the daemon-written marker safe: the daemon removes its own value only while the file still holds it, so it can never clobber a declaration the session wrote in the meantime.

heading: ## The watch-set declaration
reason: Pins the admission rule verbatim: an entry is admitted only when its checkout exists on disk AND contains a plan directory; a failing entry is silently inert rather than an error.

heading: ## Track discovery and the mapping store
reason: Pins the discovery rule's headline: one track per UNARCHIVED plan-topic directory, keyed on the directory existing — archived plans are excluded.

heading: ## Session-name derivation
reason: Pins the derivation exactly: the bare plan topic by default, with a <repo-slug>-<topic> single-dash qualifier added ONLY on a genuine cross-repository collision.

heading: ## Surface-only startup
reason: Pins 'startable, never started': a discovered plan directory with no session comes back with status 'unassigned' and tmux None — surfaced, with no session spawned for it.

heading: ## Supervised runtimes
reason: Pins the one destructive cross-runtime failure the spec designs out — a restart must resume the SAME runtime. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-25: re-pointing _do_codex_restart at the CLAUDE command turned this and two sibling tests red, then was reverted to a zero diff.

heading: ## Non-interference with tracked work
reason: Pins the startup gate that makes the whole non-interference property enforceable: the daemon verifies every watched repository ignores its scratch path and REFUSES to run if any does not, so supervision can never dirty a tracked working tree.

heading: ## Notify, never block
reason: Pins alert self-sufficiency, which is what makes a non-blocking relay usable: because the relay is the operator's only handover, every track-scoped alert names its plan topic, repository, session and pane.

heading: ## Fail-soft posture
reason: Pins the posture's sharpest clause — an unknown context reading NEVER counts as a threshold crossing, so an ambiguous reading can never trigger an act.

heading: ## The state file
reason: Pins the contract's fail-closed rule: a value outside the table ('redy') is surfaced as MALFORMED and is never read as readiness. Aptness confirmed by reading the test, not by keyword match.

heading: ## The restart interlock
reason: Pins all three deterministic checks together: an injection stamp exists (1000.0), the token is exactly 'ready', and the state mtime (1001.0) is strictly newer than the stamp — then asserts the round closes so the declaration cannot re-trigger.

heading: ## The wrap-up injection
reason: Pins the contract's ordering obligation: the stamp is readable AT PASTE TIME (seen == [1000.0]), proving it is written durably BEFORE the message is pasted, so a responding declaration always post-dates it.

heading: ## The keep-going nudge
reason: Pins the ALL-required preconditions: cleanly idle, continuously idle >= 1 hour, context above threshold, no declaration of its own — nudged exactly once, with the daemon's own marker written.

heading: ## Durable stores
reason: Pins the headline store properties: a mid-write failure leaves the old content whole (atomic replace, never truncated), removes the temp file, and warns rather than crashing (fail-soft degradation).

heading: ## Daemon invocation
reason: Pins 'NO subcommands and exactly ONE option': the invocation surface carries no store/sidecar/watch-set path flags and no recovery or interval options.

heading: ## Bootstrap preconditions
reason: Pins the refusal precondition: with $CLAUDECODE unset but inside tmux, the bootstrap refuses BEFORE any tmux mutation and names the missing precondition, so no half-set-up pane is ever created.

heading: ## Attention surface
reason: Pins the membership rule in BOTH directions: every ATTENTION_STATUSES member needs attention, and the healthy statuses do not — its own docstring notes it guards the membership test so a new status cannot be added without the block picking it up.

heading: ## Runtime requirements
reason: Pins both halves of the enforceable clause: on an unsupported host the daemon REFUSES to start naming the failed precondition, and that check runs BEFORE every other startup gate (asserted by making a watched repo ALSO fail the gitignore gate and confirming only 'unsupported host' is reported). CAVEAT: the constraint's other half — Linux+tmux as a DECLARED requirement rather than an unfinished portability story — is decision D4, implemented by core item livespec-b1uo.2 which is still backlog. This row's evidence covers the behavior, not that declaration.

heading: ## Atomicity and single instance
reason: Pins the 'at most ONE daemon instance per mapping store' half via the flock singleton, fail-closed: an uncreatable lockfile is treated as CONTENDED rather than as permission to run. The whole-file atomic-replace half of this heading is pinned by the test mapped to contracts.md 'Durable stores'.

heading: ## Acting safety
reason: Pins the heading's governing clause — every keystroke-bearing act is suppressed unless the pane is POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED as this track's supervised session. Chosen over the individual suppression tests because it is the hardest case: process and cwd both pass, only the name betrays the pane, and the act is refused even with a valid `ready` that would otherwise restart. The four never-paste cases have their own tests (busy/gate/shell/foreign) mapped nowhere else.

heading: ## Scenarios
reason: Gate-backed row, and pleasingly circular: this heading's rule IS check-heading-coverage direction 4, so the registry row for it is validated by the very check this test pins. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26 by deleting check-heading-coverage from the aggregate.

heading: ## Scenario: A wrap-up is injected when a track crosses its threshold
reason: Integration-tier: drives a real Supervisor observe-and-act round. Asserts the stamp is readable from INSIDE the paste callback (proving write-before-paste, not merely both-by-the-end), exactly ONE paste, and that the message names the state file, all three writable values and the handoff path. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: moving the stamp write to after the paste turns it red with [None] vs [1000.0].

heading: ## Scenario: The wrap-up sharpens as context keeps falling
reason: Integration-tier. Warns at 40% then crosses into 28%, asserting the first message is a suggestion and the second the insistent demand. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: setting _INSIST_AT to 0 turns it red.

heading: ## Scenario: A band never fires twice in one round
reason: Integration-tier, and it pins the scenario's BECAUSE clause rather than just its Then: the Supervisor is rebuilt from scratch between observations, standing in for the daemon restart, so a band set held only in memory would re-warn. A test reusing one Supervisor would pass on in-memory state and prove nothing. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: dropping the add_notified_band persistence turns it red.

heading: ## Scenario: A winding-down acknowledgement pauses the escalation
reason: Integration-tier. A fresh acknowledgement suppresses a wrap-up that would otherwise fire on a newly-crossed band. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: setting ACK_STALE_AFTER negative (so every ack is instantly stale) turns it red. Note a threshold of exactly 0.0 does NOT redden it — the ack's age is 0.0 and the comparison is <=, so the sabotage must go negative to land.

heading: ## Scenario: A stale acknowledgement resumes escalation but authorizes nothing
reason: Integration-tier, covering BOTH halves: escalation resumes (a lower band fires and the track is re-reported on stderr) and staleness still authorizes NOTHING. The ordering is load-bearing — the round is opened FIRST so the stamp exists, and the acknowledgement post-dates it, which forces the restart interlock all the way to its token check. An earlier draft acknowledged first and never warned; it passed because the interlock short-circuited on the missing stamp, and sabotaging ready_valid to accept winding-down left it GREEN. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26 after correction: that same sabotage now turns it red, as does the negative ACK_STALE_AFTER.

heading: ## Scenario: A fresh ready declaration triggers the atomic restart
reason: Integration-tier: opens a REAL wrap-up round (which is what writes the injection stamp), then declares `ready` post-dating it. Asserts ONE respawn and no new-session / no `/exit` send-keys (atomicity as the absence of the alternatives), the claude launch command, exactly one resume prompt naming the handoff path, and that the state file plus the round's stamp are gone. A final re-tick pins that the consumed declaration cannot re-trigger. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: skipping `_clear_state` on the success path reddens the state-file assertion (and, verified on an isolated probe, the re-trigger assertion at 2 respawns != 1); re-pointing `_launch_command` at the codex command reddens the launch-command assertion.

heading: ## Scenario: A ready declaration from a prior round never restarts
reason: Integration-tier: the declaration is written BEFORE the round is opened, so 'its mtime predates this round's stamp' is an observed consequence of the sequence rather than a hand-picked pair of numbers — the test asserts that ordering against the stamp the daemon actually wrote. Asserts the interlock refuses (no respawn, status not `restarting`) and that nothing consumes the declaration or the open round. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: dropping the mtime comparison from `signals.ready_valid` restarts the track on the prior round's declaration.

heading: ## Scenario: An uncertifiable ready declaration is surfaced as attention
reason: Integration-tier: writes a bare `ready` with NO round stamp, asserts `ready_valid(..., injection_stamp=None)` is still false, proves no respawn occurs before or after the bounded floor, then checks the attention status, row note, and stderr alert carry the age, reason, and coordinates. The sibling edge test in the same file walks quantized re-alerting, clearing, and re-arm. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED in-test: treating bare `ready` as plain `idle`, adding attention without alerting, or failing to clear the alert condition reddens one of the paired assertions.

heading: ## Scenario: A ready declaration is voided when its session resumes work
reason: Integration-tier: covers BOTH halves of the scenario over real rounds and a moving clock. A declaration younger than `MARKER_VOID_GRACE` survives the declaring turn's own busy tail and then genuinely restarts the track; one older than the grace is cleared while busy, and going idle again proves the 'instead of restarting later' clause. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: `MARKER_VOID_GRACE = 0.0` and making the void unconditional each redden the young half; `MARKER_VOID_GRACE = 10_000.0` reddens the stale half.

heading: ## Scenario: An undeclared session at the danger line is reported, never restarted
reason: Integration-tier: warns a real track, then drops it across the danger line with no declaration. Asserts the report names every coordinate (topic, repo slug, tmux session, and a copy-pasteable `tmux switch-client` jump) and says `declared NOTHING` rather than the stale-ACK wording. 'No further act' is pinned as a paste count held constant across ten further observations — the crossing's own coalesced wrap-up is authorized by the threshold, so the claim is about what happens AFTER it settles. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: `DANGER_CTX_REMAINING = 0` makes the row read `warned` with no alert; reducing `alert` to `repo::topic` reddens the coordinate assertions.

heading: ## Scenario: A malformed state value is surfaced and treated as no declaration
reason: Integration-tier, and deliberately DIFFERENTIAL: every restart precondition is satisfied over a real round (open stamp, idle settled pane, declaration post-dating the stamp) so the only difference from the fresh-`ready` scenario is the token itself — which is what makes 'no act is authorized' a claim about the value rather than about some other unmet condition. Asserts the value is surfaced by name, the round stays open, and at the danger line the track reports as having `declared NOTHING`. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: `valid_token` accepting anything silences the surfacing; `read_state` coercing an unknown token to `ready` respawns the track on a typo.

heading: ## Scenario: A blocked declaration is relayed, not answered
reason: Integration-tier: the pane is deliberately deep in the DANGER band, so `blocked` has to win a precedence contest rather than merely be the only thing happening — the same test above the threshold would pass even if `blocked` were checked last. Asserts the reason is relayed as stderr text naming every coordinate plus a jump command, and that the pane is neither keystroked nor respawned. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: removing the gate branch's `or blocked is not None` disjunct makes the track read `danger` and get a wrap-up pasted; reducing `alert` to `repo::topic` reddens the coordinate assertions.

heading: ## Scenario: An idle session with context left is nudged once per episode
reason: Integration-tier: walks the whole episode lifecycle on one track — below the one-hour floor nothing is keystroked, past it exactly one keep-going message is pasted and the daemon's own marker is written, a further idle tick does not re-nudge, the session working clears the marker, and a fresh hour earns a second nudge. The paste is asserted as a NUDGE (`_wrapup_count` held at zero), since the wrap-up travels the same paste path and means the opposite; the marker is checked by TOKEN, so a marker written as `ready` would redden here rather than silently arming a restart. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: `IDLE_NUDGE_AFTER = 0.0`, dropping the once-per-episode guard, and making `_clear_idle_nudge_state` a no-op each redden a different leg.

heading: ## Scenario: An unassigned plan is discovered but never auto-started
reason: Integration-tier: drives `tick(act=True)` — the ACTING path, the only one where surface-only has content, since `act=False` cannot launch anything by construction and asserting there would be vacuous. Ten ticks rather than one: 'never auto-started' is a claim about a daemon observing the same startable plan forever, and one observation cannot tell 'never launches' from 'launches on the second look'. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: making `auto_link` create the session it fails to find starts a session for a plan nobody asked to start.

heading: ## Scenario: The supervision-artifact existence probe is liveness-gated and existence-only
reason: Integration-tier: the two NEGATIVE clauses are asserted by instrumenting `pathlib.Path` — `open`/`read_text`/`read_bytes` raise for that one basename — because 'did not read a file' leaves no trace in a result, so a read fails hard at the moment it happens. `exists` is recorded UNFILTERED, so an empty log cannot be mistaken for a skipped probe: the assertion is that the handoff file is ABSENT from a log still showing other file work. The liveness gate is exercised by DIFFERENCE on the same repo and file — the live-session pass must probe it and the dead-session pass must not. Asserting only the absence would pass against a daemon that never probes at all, a different bug wearing the same green tick. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: making the probe `read_text()` trips the patched reader; probing from `_no_managed_pane_row` reddens the dead-session assertion.

heading: ## Scenario: Topics colliding across repositories get qualified session names
reason: Integration-tier, asserted through `auto_link` rather than through `registry.tmux_id`: the unit tier already pins the naming function, and what was unpinned above it is that the daemon computes the collision set from the DISCOVERY pass and derives names with it. Real plan directories in two repos, tmux sessions served under BOTH the qualified and the retired bare name, and `tick` decides which it recognizes — serving the bare `shared` session is what gives this teeth, since a daemon ignoring the collision set would match its cwd and link it. The single dash is checked literally, because `<slug>--<topic>` would still satisfy a substring assertion. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: `colliding_topics` returning an empty frozenset links the bare session instead of the qualified one.

heading: ## Scenario: The daemon refuses an unsupported host
reason: Integration-tier: drives the real `run(once=True)` startup path. The ORDERING clause is the substantive half and is asserted by failing ALL THREE gates at once — no /proc, an un-ignored scratch path, and a singleton lock already held — so the assertion is not merely that the host reason appears but that the other two do NOT. Testing the host gate alone cannot distinguish 'first' from 'only one failing'. The three refusal tests share a CONTROL (`test_scenario_the_fixture_track_is_warned_when_every_startup_gate_passes`) proving the same fixture pastes a wrap-up when nothing is refused; without it, 'no wrap-up' would be satisfied by a daemon that never warns anything. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: moving the host gate below the gitignore gate, and `unsupported_host_reasons` returning [], each let a different gate speak.

heading: ## Scenario: The daemon refuses a repository that does not ignore its scratch path
reason: Integration-tier: TWO repos are watched and only one offends, because naming the offender is the whole point of the clause — with a single watched repo a message that named the wrong repo, or every repo, would still contain the right string. The three refusal tests share a CONTROL (`test_scenario_the_fixture_track_is_warned_when_every_startup_gate_passes`) proving the same fixture pastes a wrap-up when nothing is refused; without it, 'no wrap-up' would be satisfied by a daemon that never warns anything. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: `unignored_tmp_repos` returning [] starts the daemon; returning the full watch set names the innocent repo too.

heading: ## Scenario: A second daemon instance refuses to start
reason: Integration-tier: the lock is taken by ACQUIRING it the way the daemon does rather than by writing a sentinel — `flock` locks belong to the open file description, so a second open+flock contends even inside one process, which exercises the real mechanism. The second half (releasing the lock lets a daemon start and warn) is what proves the refusal was the LOCK's doing; without it a daemon broken some other way would look identical. The three refusal tests share a CONTROL (`test_scenario_the_fixture_track_is_warned_when_every_startup_gate_passes`) proving the same fixture pastes a wrap-up when nothing is refused; without it, 'no wrap-up' would be satisfied by a daemon that never warns anything. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: a SHARED flock lets the second instance supervise; dropping the lock path from the message reddens the naming assertion.

heading: ## Scenario: A dropped resume submission is retried without a second kill
reason: Integration-tier: the drop is modelled where it happens — a respawn hook leaves the pane showing a box that HOLDS the resume text, which is what a fresh TUI that swallowed the Enter looks like. `paste_ok = False` would be a failed paste: a different fault with the same return value that never produces the stranded box this scenario is about. 'Never kills it again' is a respawn count of ONE across the whole sequence, including ticks where a still-valid `ready` marker is sitting right there — that marker is the danger, since without the retry interception the `elif ready:` branch would respawn-kill the fresh session every tick. The closing phase (the box clears, the round closes) is what makes 'until the prompt lands' a claim rather than a description of an infinite retry. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: the retry branch re-entering `_do_restart` pushes the respawn count to 2; clearing the state on a failed submit hides the stranding.

heading: ## Scenario: A restart never switches a track's runtime
reason: Integration-tier, BOTH directions, since the clause is symmetric. This is the one place a bug in this daemon is DESTRUCTIVE rather than merely wrong: aiming `claude -n <topic>` at a codex pane replaces the codex session and orphans its rollout. The codex half drives a REAL round rather than seeding the stamp — the wrap-up is pasted and the pane made to go BUSY in response, which is how a codex submit is confirmed (codex has no empty-box signal). A hand-seeded round would skip the runtime-aware submit, which is part of what 'supervised under one agent runtime' means. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: inverting `_do_restart`'s dispatch, and replacing `_codex_launch_command` with `_launch_command`, each issue the claude command at the codex pane.

heading: ## Scenario: An unknown context reading never triggers a wrap-up
reason: Integration-tier over two tracks, because the clauses describe different states. The track that HAD a reading takes it deliberately ABOVE the threshold, so that treating unknown as a low or zero percentage — the natural way to get this wrong — would cross and warn; below the threshold it would warn either way and prove nothing. The track that NEVER had one is where 'renders as unknown rather than a guess' is observable, and it is asserted through `Supervisor.render` rather than on `view.ctx`, because the clause is about what the OPERATOR sees: a row carrying None that printed as `0%` would satisfy a field assertion and still mislead. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 2026-07-26: `_effective_ctx` returning the raw reading erases the last known value; rendering the unknown cell as `0%` reddens the never-known assertion.
